title: Of 19 performance PRs, 16 keep types and values the same; two change a result in a corner, and one is a spike
sub: Cyrus asked whether the performance PRs compromise the correctness of typing or evaluation, and for more analysis and coverage of functional correctness. For each of the 19 PRs against #2609 (the performance tracking issue), this report says what it caches, skips or shares; why the result is the same as without it, or where it is not; what that rests on; and which tests back it and which are missing. For the meeting with Cyrus on 2026-10-21.
as_of: As of 2026-10-19, each PR read at its head (commit ids below). Two corners were confirmed by running the PR against its parent; the rest is from reading the code.
answers: 16 of the 19 keep every type and value the same. 4 are tests and budgets that cannot change a result; 5 hold outright; 7 hold under an assumption stated with each (below).

2 change a result in a corner, both confirmed by running. #2610's load fallback, when it splits a long program just after an operand, loads x - y as x ¿ - y: a new hole, and the minus turned unary, saved back on the next edit. #2651 changes what a module under a one-member signature evaluates to (an ill-typed program, and the new value looks like the right one), and drops an error for a module that names itself.
1 is a spike, not for merging: #2490 (the evaluator compiled to WebAssembly) removes the builtin livelits to build. It is a draft and says so.

The assumptions worth naming: three PRs treat a structural hash as equality (#2661 and #2681 a 60-bit type hash, #2673 a 64-bit term hash), so a collision would silently give a wrong answer; #2673's hash has a structure that makes some collisions easier than chance. #2606 relies on every finished incremental cache being consistent. All rely on terms never being mutated in place.

The biggest gap is in the tests, not the PRs. The property that compares incremental evaluation with evaluation from scratch is switched off on dev (#2457), and no test runs a program with an optimization on and off and compares. A tests PR to dev can add both (below).
fig_alt: The 19 PRs in four columns by area (statics, evaluator, parsing and editor, tests and CI), each a box coloured by its verdict.
fig_caption: Each PR by area, coloured by its verdict. Statics' column holds the PRs that change statics or the evaluator's ascriptions; the tests column holds test, budget and CI PRs, three of them stacked on runtime PRs. Each box links to its section.
prs_intro: For each PR: what it changes, its mechanism, why the result is the same, what that assumes, where it is weakest, and its tests. Three PRs in the tests column (#2689, #2690, #2691) are stacked on others, so their diffs include those PRs' code; their own commits are test-only. #2681's branch also merges #2661 and #2679.
tests:
What the tests check today. Each PR adds hand-made cases for what it changes, most of them checking values. The step-budget tests (#2678, #2690) also check their programs' values, so a stale reuse there would fail; the pass-count and byte budgets (#2689, #2691) check cost only. dev has 41 hand-made incremental-evaluation tests and property tests, but its property that compares incremental evaluation with evaluation from scratch after an edit is disabled, because of a known bug (#2457: a binding left unsubstituted when evaluation gets stuck after an edited literal). No test runs the corpus of programs with an optimization on and off and compares the results.

What to add, in a tests PR to dev:

  1. Turn the incremental-against-fresh property back on for completed results (stuck results skipped until #2457 is fixed), with a fixed seed, and with a generator that also makes recursive lets and modules of recursive helpers: the programs #2675 and #2606 reuse more of.
  2. A corpus comparison: every program in hazel-programs (the slides, the tutorial), evaluated incrementally after an edit and from scratch, and analyzed with each statics optimization on and off: types, error marks, elaborations (ignoring ids), values, probe samples and test results compared.
  3. Hash checks: for the type hash and the term hash, a property that equal hashes imply equal terms (up to ids and provenance), and a census of every type and subterm in the corpus.
  4. A parser comparison: the load fallback against character-by-character typing, with each corpus program padded by 0 to 99 characters so that every top-level space is a split point at some offset (this finds #2610's case).
  5. Budget tests that check results too: the pass-count and byte budgets already analyze and evaluate their programs; asserting the types and values makes them correctness tests at no cost.

Each PR's own missing tests are in its section above.
next: Fix #2610 before it merges: remold the joined pieces once before the final re-grout (or split only where the next token cannot change mold), and add the padded split-position sweep. Done at 94ca8a2daa (the remold, and three split cases; the sweep is still to add).

In #2651, say that a module under a one-member signature now evaluates to the module itself (and keep it, with a test); restore the error for a module definition that names itself. Done at 29c08fd8fa, and said in the description.
Strengthen the hashes: a finalizer per lane for #2673's term hash, which removes the bit-31 cancellation, and either a wider type hash or an equality check behind the hit for #2661 and #2681.
Open the tests PR to dev (the five items above), starting with the incremental-against-fresh property.
In #2675's description, mention the unused-variable warning it now gives for a binding a recursive let shadows; in #2673's, that its reuse decisions differ from the old check in two corners.
method: How each PR was read: its description, its diff and its own commits, at its head (the commit beside each section), with files at that head read where the diff alone was not enough, on 2026-10-19. Four read-only reviews ran side by side: statics (with the evaluator's ascriptions), the evaluator, parsing and the editor, and the test and CI PRs. They built and ran nothing.

What was run: the two corners that change a result, with Hazel's command-line tool (format, run) at the PR's head and at its parent: #2651 at e3013b0360 and 34f9605ddf; #2610 at 0aba66119a and its parent.
What was not checked: each PR's own tests were not run here (their CI is green); the other corners named in the sections are from reading.
